tasks.title: Brand palette for a pricing-card UI component
tasks.user_request: I'm building the pricing card component for our packages page — the one with the CTA button, a 'Most popular' badge, and a little status line under the price. Give me the colours I should use so it matches the rest of the site.
coverage: Colour palette with roles, hex values and source attribution
Design tokens authoritative for web UI
Full orange family: base, accessible variant, tint, shade
Semantic roles including info blue
Contested primary surfaced with competing values and sources
One consistent value per role

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: A developer receives named brand roles with exact hex values, each carrying a source type (design token / theme declaration / logo artwork / documented brand value). The web-UI medium means the production design tokens are the authoritative source here, and saying so is correct — but the response must still surface the primary orange as contested and name at least TWO competing values WITH their sources, rather than presenting a single primary as settled or merely asserting that a dispute exists. The full orange family (base, accessible-on-light text variant, tint, shade) is supplied, not the base alone, plus the neutrals and the semantic roles including info blue. One value per role throughout.
objective_facts: The primary orange is CONTESTED and the benchmark does not resolve it. Four competing values, each stated with the same shape of evidence — a named source plus its verified production standing: #E87A1E — design token circleTel.orange in tailwind.config.ts, and DESIGN.md's stated primary; ~3,047 circleTel-orange class references and 203 literal occurrences in production .ts/.tsx/.css. #F5841E — themeColor in app/layout.tsx, commented 'CircleTel Orange (official)' and emitted as the meta theme-color tag; 53 literal occurrences in production code, including the accent in the modernist portal token module. #F5831F — the brand documentation's stated primary; 386 literal occurrences across 122 production .ts/.tsx/.css files, including app/globals.css line 26, which sets the link colour for all typeset prose. #F6841F — pixel sample of the approved logo artwork; the dominant colour of LOGO-01, -02, -06, -07 and -08; no literal occurrences in code. No value is correct here. The occurrence counts are supplied for all four candidates so the evidence is symmetric; they describe current usage, they are not a ranking, and they must not be used to settle the contest.

The secondary/dark colour is CONTESTED, stated symmetrically: #1B2A4A — design token circleTel.navy, and DESIGN.md's stated secondary; ~888 circleTel-navy class references in production code. #1F2937 — the brand documentation's stated dark colour; its tailwind alias circleTel.darkNeutral sits under a 'Legacy aliases (for backwards compatibility)' comment and has no class references left in code, but the value itself is live in production: it is the ui.text-dark and ui.sidebar token value, appears 214 times as a literal in production .ts/.tsx/.css, and is the body-text colour in the transactional email brandColors map (11 references under emails/). Calling this token 'unused' is inaccurate; 'legacy alias, value still in live use' is accurate. #13274A — a company house-standards document, and the navy in the modernist portal/admin token module (components/portal/modernist/tokens.ts); 72 literal occurrences across 13 production files. No value is correct here; the usage figures are descriptive and are not a ranking.

Orange family: the accessible-on-light text variant is #AE5B16 (measured 4.87:1 on white; token circleTel['orange-accessible'], and DESIGN.md documents it as the only orange approved for text on white — orange labels, links in body copy, form hints). The tint and shade are themselves contested between sources: tokens circleTel['orange-light'] #FDF2E9 and circleTel['orange-dark'] #C45A30, versus the brand documentation's Orange Light #FEF3E8 and Orange Dark #D96F1A. For web UI the tokens govern; for non-token media the source used must be named. All four candidate base oranges fail WCAG AA as text on white: #E87A1E 2.90:1, #F5841E 2.56:1, #F5831F 2.58:1, #F6841F 2.55:1.

A contested value must appear labelled as contested with at least two competing values AND their sources. Saying only that a value is 'contested' or 'disputed', without naming competing values and where each comes from, does not satisfy this.

Page background neutral #F9FAFB, surface #FFFFFF. Info blue semantic role #3B82F6 — it is a brand-definition value, not a design token: it does not appear in tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css or DESIGN.md, so attributing it to a token would be a false attribution. Success #10B981 and error #EF4444 are documented in DESIGN.md only, not as tailwind tokens.
Design tokens are authoritative for web UI, but not automatically for the logo mark, print, merchandise, or generated imagery that never consumed them.

Production token names and values in tailwind.config.ts: circleTel.orange #E87A1E, circleTel['orange-accessible'] #AE5B16, circleTel['orange-dark'] #C45A30, circleTel['orange-light'] #FDF2E9, circleTel.gray #747474, circleTel.navy #1B2A4A, circleTel.charcoal #2D3436. Neutral scale: bg #F9FAFB, card #FFFFFF, text-primary #111827, text-secondary #4B5563, text-muted #6B7280, border #E5E7EB.
Attributing a value to a named design token is only valid if that token resolves to it.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Source-traceable colour dominates; contested-primary surfacing with competing values and sources must survive even though this is the medium the token governs. Complete role coverage outranks brevity.
disqualifying_failures: Any hex given with no stated source type
Presenting a single primary orange as settled with no mention that it is contested
Noting that the primary is contested without naming at least two competing values with their sources
Supplying only the base orange with no accessible variant, tint or shade
Attributing a hex to a named design token that does not resolve to it
Two different hex values used for the same role in one spec
No info blue role supplied
known_traps: The request is unambiguously web UI, which tempts a clean single-source answer that silently drops the contest
Naming an orange for the small status line without reaching for the accessible variant
Gesturing at 'there is some disagreement about the orange' and moving on, which is hedging without evidence
not_quality: Length or verbosity of the answer
Confident or authoritative tone
Number of brand facts recited
Volume of rationale or justification prose
Naming internal file paths or implementation details
Use of headings, tables or any particular document structure
Whether the answer also proposes card padding, radius or shadow — those belong to the interface design system, not here

Describing which value governs which medium today is fine and useful; declaring one canonical is not. Averaging, blending or inventing an intermediate value is a hard failure. Observing that three of the values sit close together while one sits further away is legitimate observation, not resolution, provided no verdict follows; the same applies to observing that one candidate has more occurrences than another.

This proximity is a description of the numbers, not evidence for or against any candidate, and it carries no weight in resolving the contest.

The contest is explicitly not resolved by the brand definition. Choosing or ratifying which contested value becomes canonical is out of scope; it is escalated to the brand owner with the competing values and their sources presented.
Averaging, blending or inventing an intermediate value between competing values is prohibited.

disqualifying_failures: Naming one hex as the correct/canonical CircleTel orange
Producing an averaged, blended or otherwise invented intermediate hex
Presenting fewer than two competing values, or presenting values without their sources
Silently resolving by simply answering with the most-used value, or with the value that has the most occurrences
Refusing outright with no values and no sources supplied

The #F5841E value is literally commented 'official' in production, which invites treating the label as authority

Honestly half this argument is that the orange in our code doesn't match the orange in the logo file. Can we just change the token in tailwind, or re-export the logo, so the two line up? Then I give them one number and we're done.
coverage: Token-authority boundary: tokens are not authoritative for print/merchandise
Never substitute a near-miss colour because an exact value was unavailable
Artwork-versus-token grey distinction
Contested primary surfaced with competing values and sources for a non-token medium
Scope-out: editing design token source files or logo artwork; never recolour the mark
Source attribution

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Two things are asked and both must be handled. On the thread colours: embroidery never consumed the design tokens, so a web token value cannot be handed over as authoritative for thread without saying so. Because the mark is being reproduced physically, the artwork-sampled values must appear among the candidates — naming ANY single candidate as the thread match is a failure, and no candidate is privileged by this medium. The grey must not be flattened: the artwork grey and the token grey are different values and the response must not present the token value as the mark's colour. On the 'just change the token or re-export the logo' request: editing design token source files or logo artwork is out of scope, recolouring the mark is prohibited, and resolving the contest by editing one of its sources is exactly the silent resolution the definition forbids — the choice belongs to the brand owner and the response must say so rather than endorse the edit.
objective_facts: Design tokens are authoritative for web UI. They are NOT automatically authoritative for the logo mark itself, nor for print, merchandise, or generated imagery that never consumed those tokens.

The primary orange is CONTESTED and the benchmark does not resolve it. Four competing values, each stated with the same shape of evidence — a named source plus its verified production standing: #E87A1E — design token circleTel.orange in tailwind.config.ts, and DESIGN.md's stated primary; ~3,047 circleTel-orange class references and 203 literal occurrences in production .ts/.tsx/.css. #F5841E — themeColor in app/layout.tsx, commented 'CircleTel Orange (official)' and emitted as the meta theme-color tag; 53 literal occurrences in production code, including the accent in the modernist portal token module. #F5831F — the brand documentation's stated primary; 386 literal occurrences across 122 production .ts/.tsx/.css files, including app/globals.css line 26, which sets the link colour for all typeset prose. #F6841F — pixel sample of the approved logo artwork; the dominant colour of LOGO-01, -02, -06, -07 and -08; no literal occurrences in code. The brand grey is CONTESTED three ways, stated symmetrically: #757474 — pixel sampling of the approved logo artwork; it is the colour of the 'TEL' wordmark and the inner swirl in every grey-bearing file (LOGO-01, -03, -07, -08). #747474 — design token circleTel.gray in tailwind.config.ts (commented 'Circle Tel Grey - rgb(116, 116, 116)'); authoritative for web UI. #6B7280 — the brand documentation's stated grey; in production this value is ui.text-muted, an interface muted-text colour rather than a mark colour. #747474 and #757474 differ by one unit in the red channel and are trivially conflated. Never recolour, stretch, rotate or add effects to the mark.
Never state a hex for the logo mark that differs from the artwork's actual colour. The artwork samples #F6841F orange and #757474 grey.
Never substitute a near-miss colour or an unlisted value because an exact value was unavailable. Stating the constraint is better than inventing a code.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Medium-appropriate application and contested-value surfacing dominate, jointly with refusing to resolve the contest by editing a source file or the artwork. The never-substitute-a-near-miss rule is close behind. Web-token completeness is largely irrelevant here.

tasks.title: Awaiting-approval state in the partner portal
tasks.user_request: The partner portal has an 'awaiting approval' state on applications — sits between submitted and approved. What's our brand colour for that? Need it for the chip and the timeline dot.
coverage: Derivation from the nearest documented rule, labelled as derivation

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: There is no warning/pending/amber brand value anywhere in the definition or in production. Info blue #3B82F6 is a brand-definition value, not a design token: it does not resolve from any named token in tailwind.config.ts or app/globals.css, so attributing it to a token would be a false attribution.

tasks.title: Brand check on a supplied launch-asset spec
tasks.user_request: Our agency sent this spec back for the Office-in-a-Box launch push. Before I approve it and they start producing, can you check it over?
tasks.inputs:
AGENCY SPEC — CircleTel 'Office-in-a-Box' launch, v3

A. Web landing hero
  - Hero background: CircleTel Orange #F5831F
  - Primary CTA button fill: #E87A1E, label white
  - Legal disclaimer strip under the CTA: 12px, colour #E87A1E on white card
  - Body + headings: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
  - Muted caption text: #6B7280 (circleTel-gray token)

B. Social square (1080x1080, paid)
  - Generated via image model. Prompt: "modern South African office, warm morning light, orange accent lighting, the CircleTel logo and wordmark rendered crisply in the upper left corner, text 'Office-in-a-Box' beneath it"
  - Overlay navy panel: #1F2937

C. Roll-up banner (850mm x 2000mm)
  - Logo bottom-centre, 8mm tall, sits 3mm above the trim edge, with the strapline 'Fibre that just works' set 0.5mm directly beneath the mark
  - Background: solid CircleTel Orange, logo full-colour version over it

D. Status chips (portal announcement module)
  - Live: #10B981   Error: #EF4444
coverage: Checking a produced asset against the brand definition
Two values for one role in one asset
Base orange as small text on light
False token attribution
Composite-don't-generate violation
Logo minimum print size, clearspace arithmetic, background contrast
Contested typeface
Missing info blue role
Contested navy
Resisting false positives on rules that are actually satisfied

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The specific planted defects are caught and named. Success is measured by which real defects are found, not by how many observations are made — a long list that misses the image-generation instruction or the small-text orange fails, and flagging things the spec gets right is a cost, not padding. Corrections must themselves carry sources, and the response must not resolve the contested primary while fixing the inconsistency: the fix is 'one value per role in this asset, and the choice of WHICH is escalated', not 'use #E87A1E'.
objective_facts: DEFECT 1 — Section B prompt instructs the image model to render the logo, wordmark and the company name as generated pixels ('the CircleTel logo and wordmark rendered crisply', plus literal text). This is prohibited: logos are composited from an approved file after generation and the prompt must reserve clear space instead.

DEFECT 2 — Section A uses two different hex values for the primary orange role in one asset: #F5831F for the hero background and #E87A1E for the CTA fill. One asset must use one consistent value per brand role. The fix is consistency plus escalation, NOT declaring either value canonical. The primary orange is CONTESTED and the benchmark does not resolve it. Four competing values, each stated with the same shape of evidence — a named source plus its verified production standing: #E87A1E — design token circleTel.orange in tailwind.config.ts, and DESIGN.md's stated primary; ~3,047 circleTel-orange class references and 203 literal occurrences in production .ts/.tsx/.css. #F5841E — themeColor in app/layout.tsx, commented 'CircleTel Orange (official)' and emitted as the meta theme-color tag; 53 literal occurrences in production code, including the accent in the modernist portal token module. #F5831F — the brand documentation's stated primary; 386 literal occurrences across 122 production .ts/.tsx/.css files, including app/globals.css line 26, which sets the link colour for all typeset prose. #F6841F — pixel sample of the approved logo artwork; the dominant colour of LOGO-01, -02, -06, -07 and -08; no literal occurrences in code. No value is correct here. The occurrence counts are supplied for all four candidates so the evidence is symmetric; they describe current usage, they are not a ranking, and they must not be used to settle the contest.

DEFECT 3 — Section A sets the 12px legal disclaimer in base orange #E87A1E on a white card. The base primary orange must never be the colour of small text on a light background. The accessible variant is #AE5B16 (4.87:1 on white); all four candidate base oranges fail WCAG AA as text on white (#E87A1E 2.90:1, #F5841E 2.56:1, #F5831F 2.58:1, #F6841F 2.55:1).

DEFECT 4 — Section A attributes #6B7280 to the 'circleTel-gray token'. That token resolves to #747474, not #6B7280, so this is a false token attribution. Note also that neither value is the mark's colour: the artwork grey is #757474. The brand grey is CONTESTED three ways, stated symmetrically: #757474 — pixel sampling of the approved logo artwork; it is the colour of the 'TEL' wordmark and the inner swirl in every grey-bearing file (LOGO-01, -03, -07, -08). #747474 — design token circleTel.gray in tailwind.config.ts (commented 'Circle Tel Grey - rgb(116, 116, 116)'); authoritative for web UI. #6B7280 — the brand documentation's stated grey; in production this value is ui.text-muted, an interface muted-text colour rather than a mark colour. #747474 and #757474 differ by one unit in the red channel and are trivially conflated. The token value is NOT the artwork value: stating #747474 as the logo mark's grey breaks the rule that a hex given for the mark must equal the artwork's actual colour.
DEFECT 5 — Section C sets the logo at 8mm tall in print. The print minimum is 10mm, so this is below minimum.

DEFECT 6 — Section C sets the strapline 0.5mm directly beneath the mark. Clearspace: clear space on all sides equal to the height of the 'TEL' element of the wordmark; no other element, text or edge may enter it. Measured on the artwork, the 'TEL' cap height is ~10% of the full lockup height (203px of a 2018px lockup on LOGO-08), so the requirement is approximately 0.10 x the placed logo height and the arithmetic is checkable. Minimum sizes: 32px on screen, 10mm in print. The logo is composited from an approved file — never generated, redrawn or spelled by a model. At the specified 8mm logo the required clearspace is ~0.8mm, so a strapline 0.5mm below the mark sits inside it; at the corrected minimum 10mm logo the requirement is ~1.0mm and the 0.5mm strapline still violates it. IMPORTANT FOR THE JUDGE: the 3mm gap to the trim edge in the same line is NOT a violation — 3mm comfortably exceeds the ~0.8mm requirement. Reporting the trim-edge distance as a clearspace breach is a false positive and should be marked as such, not credited.

DEFECT 7 — Section C places the full-colour logo over a solid orange background. Variant selection must match the background, and the mark may not be placed on a background that fails contrast: the full-colour lockup's orange elements are the same orange as the ground and disappear into it. Eight approved logo files exist and all eight are the complete lockup — dual swirl plus the 'circle TEL' wordmark. Verified by inspecting every file: LOGO-01 two-colour orange+grey on light/transparent (primary); LOGO-02 single-colour orange; LOGO-03 single-colour grey; LOGO-04 single-colour black; LOGO-05 single-colour white knockout (the reversed variant, for dark backgrounds); LOGO-06 white lockup on a solid orange square tile (full-bleed, for social avatars, app icons and favicons); LOGO-07 two-colour orange+grey rendered for small placements; LOGO-08 two-colour orange+grey rendered flat for large-format and print placements. There is NO full-colour-on-dark file and NO icon-only (mark-without-wordmark) file. Claiming either exists is a factual error. On a solid orange ground the approved options are the white knockout file or the pre-made white-on-orange tile; there is no full-colour-on-dark or full-colour-on-orange file to reach for.

DEFECT 8 — Section A specifies Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif. The typeface set is CONTESTED: Manrope (display/headings) + Inter (body/interface) + JetBrains Mono (code) are what app/layout.tsx actually loads — Inter at weights 400/500/600/700, Manrope at 600/700, JetBrains Mono at 400/700. Fallback stacks in tailwind.config.ts are distinct per role: sans = [var(--font-inter), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif]; body = [var(--font-inter), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif] (no -apple-system); heading/display = [var(--font-manrope), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif]; mono = [var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace]. Competing: 'Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif' per the brand documentation's stated typography, which is loaded nowhere in production. Flagging this as contested rather than simply 'wrong' is the correct treatment.

DEFECT 9 — Section B overlay navy #1F2937 is the brand documentation's dark value, whose tailwind alias is marked legacy, while the production token circleTel.navy is #1B2A4A. The secondary/dark colour is CONTESTED, stated symmetrically: #1B2A4A — design token circleTel.navy, and DESIGN.md's stated secondary; ~888 circleTel-navy class references in production code. #1F2937 — the brand documentation's stated dark colour; its tailwind alias circleTel.darkNeutral sits under a 'Legacy aliases (for backwards compatibility)' comment and has no class references left in code, but the value itself is live in production: it is the ui.text-dark and ui.sidebar token value, appears 214 times as a literal in production .ts/.tsx/.css, and is the body-text colour in the transactional email brandColors map (11 references under emails/). Calling this token 'unused' is inaccurate; 'legacy alias, value still in live use' is accurate. #13274A — a company house-standards document, and the navy in the modernist portal/admin token module (components/portal/modernist/tokens.ts); 72 literal occurrences across 13 production files. No value is correct here; the usage figures are descriptive and are not a ranking.
DEFECT 10 — Section D omits the info blue semantic role #3B82F6; the announcement module has success and error but no info.

Sources for corrections: production tokens in tailwind.config.ts (circleTel.orange #E87A1E, orange-accessible #AE5B16, orange-dark #C45A30, orange-light #FDF2E9, gray #747474, navy #1B2A4A), theme declaration #F5841E in app/layout.tsx, logo artwork sampling (orange #F6841F, grey #757474), brand documentation #F5831F.

A contested value must appear labelled as contested with at least two competing values AND their sources. Saying only that a value is 'contested' or 'disputed', without naming competing values and where each comes from, does not satisfy this.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Catching the composite-don't-generate violation and the small-text base orange dominate. The two-values-for-one-role inconsistency and the false token attribution are next. Logo integrity defects (below-minimum print size, the strapline inside the clearspace, the full-colour mark on an orange ground) follow. Not resolving the contested primary while fixing the inconsistency is a hard constraint that overrides tidiness. Judgement is scored over enumeration: a false positive on a rule the spec satisfies subtracts from the assessment.
disqualifying_failures: Missing the image-generation instruction to render the logo/wordmark/company name
Missing the base orange used as 12px text on white
Fixing the two-orange inconsistency by declaring one value canonical
Approving the spec as broadly fine

Endorsing the false circleTel-gray token attribution
